profile.purpose: Documents buying a pair of Levi's 501 Shrink-to-Fit raw denim jeans and shrinking them by soaking and air-drying. It compares them on body with thrifted Gap 1969 selvedge jeans and worn Levi's 511s, and checks the fit again after one week.
profile.thesis: Levi's 501 STF are a cheap, classic entry point into raw denim. The video shows how a hot soak and air-dry changes their fit, and how they stretch over the first week.
key_takeaways: The creator explains how he got into raw denim after a friend's Naked & Famous jeans, and says he previously would not spend more than about $100 on jeans.
He found thrifted Gap 1969 Japanese selvedge raw jeans with tags for $11 and paid about $30 for the Levi's 501 STF.
Modern 501s are described as non-selvedge with cheaper construction than older 501s, while Levi's is presented as the original jean brand.
Levi's sizing advice is to size up one or two in the waist and go longer in length. The creator did not follow it, relying on reports that the waist stretches.
The 501, 511 and Gap jeans are modeled on body, with a basic cuff and a pin roll.
The soak used water as hot as possible, with bowls to keep the jeans submerged. The planned one hour was cut to 20 to 30 minutes after reading online.
Drying outdoors in sun and wind took about two hours versus about nine hours indoors. Opening the legs improves airflow.
After drying, the waist was very tight while the length barely changed. A week later the waist and thighs had stretched.
The creator tapered the legs before the follow-up and notes a seam was splitting on the second day, a sign of cheaper construction.

outline.title: Introduction to denim
outline.summary: How the creator got into raw denim through a friend's Naked & Famous jeans and denim jackets, despite previously not wanting to spend much on jeans.

outline.title: Thrifting raw denim
outline.summary: His belief in thrifting and his find of tagged Gap 1969 Japanese selvedge raw jeans for $11, including a look at the selvedge and his rough self-hem.

outline.title: Levi's 501 analysis
outline.summary: Compares colors with the Gap jeans and discusses viewer claims that 501s aren't made like they used to be, the non-selvedge construction and the ~$30 price. Also covers Levi's sizing advice and shrinking methods.

outline.title: Modeling the jeans
outline.summary: Tries on the Gap 1969, the worn Levi's 511s and the unshrunk 501 STF. Shows the 501s uncut, with a basic cuff and with a pin roll.

outline.title: Shrink-to-fit plan
outline.summary: In the bathroom he explains filling the tub with the hottest water possible and using three bowls to keep the jeans submerged, initially for an hour.

outline.title: The soaking process
outline.summary: He shortens the soak to 20 to 30 minutes and notes the blue indigo in the water and the claim that soaking strengthens the denim. He also gives a 'cotton kills' warning about wet cotton.

outline.title: Drying the denim
outline.summary: Hangs the jeans outside in the sun and opens the legs for airflow to speed up drying.

outline.title: Results and final fit
outline.summary: The jeans dried in about two hours. He tries them on, finding the waist very tight and the length barely changed, then cuffs them and gives his impressions.

outline.title: One week follow-up
outline.summary: A week later the waist and thighs have stretched enough to wear a belt. He discloses he tapered the legs and notes a seam was splitting early on.

corrections.note: Changes the planned one-hour soak (segment 7) to 20 to 30 minutes after reading that an hour is overkill.
After first saying the jeans didn't look like they had shrunk much (segment 11), he says they definitely did slim up, mainly in the waist, though length barely changed.
Discloses that he tapered the legs before the one-week follow-up, so the slimmer lower leg is not from shrinking or stretching.
